questions.question: How should the activation list work?

options.label: Allowlist (opt-in)
options.description: Only dirs listed in the file get servers. New dirs under ~/dev are dormant until you add them. Safest — keeps the count minimal.

options.label: Denylist (opt-out)
options.description: Every subdir gets a server unless listed. New dirs spawn automatically; you blacklist the ones you don't want.

options.label: Per-dir marker file
options.description: Each dir opts in by containing a `.claude-remote-control` marker file. No central list — lives with the repo.

questions.question: Which dirs should be active right now?

options.label: mm-dev (root)
options.description: The ~/dev root itself — useful for cross-project work

Let me look at the current LaunchAgent setup to understand what's spawning.

Got it. Currently the supervisor in `remote-control-supervisor.sh:39-56` auto-spawns a server for `~/dev` root + every immediate subdir. You have 7 subdirs + the root, so 8 servers running.

The cleanest design is to add an activation file the supervisor reads each tick, plus a skill to edit it.
